blockers.description: WR-01 unanswered: RANGE_MARKER is the literal "@^", so only caret ranges split off a bare string. "foo@~1.0.0" parses as name=foo, marketplace=~1.0.0, fails the token allowlist, and drops the whole element. When every element is unusable the line is omitted — byte-identical to a plugin declaring no dependencies. Three options were posed (add a closed-set reason token / document the limit and keep silence / widen the range marker); the operator asked a clarifying question about version handling instead and the question was never re-posed.
blockers.workaround: WR-01 part 1 (correct the VERSION_PATTERN doc comment, which claims ~1.2, >=1.0, 1.x and || are reachable via the bare-string form when only ^ is) is uncontroversial and can land without the decision. Part 2 (distinguish 'declared none' from 'declared only unusable') needs the call because it adds a catalog state.
